title: Design System: Button Counter — The Obi Band

display.purpose: The eternal count, and the visitor's personal count on the Yours pane. Never anything else.

headline.purpose: The Button Counter wordmark, repeated on the spine and every obi band.

title.purpose: Pane section titles: The record, Yours, Colophon.

body.purpose: The single reading paragraph — the synthetic-data disclosure in the colophon.

label.purpose: Every annotative micro-caption: count label, button caption, pane metadata, catalog, barcode, axis ticks.

credits-jp.purpose: Bilingual vertical credit columns on the obi band.

shadows.name: disc-rest
shadows.value: 0 0.14rem 0.24rem -0.06rem color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 40%, transparent), 0 0.5rem 0.7rem -0.28rem color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 34%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Press disc at rest — contact shadow plus short ambient cast.

shadows.name: disc-hover
shadows.value: 0 0.22rem 0.34rem -0.04rem color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 42%, transparent), 0 0.85rem 1.05rem -0.15rem color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 36%, transparent)

shadows.name: disc-active
shadows.value: 0 0.05rem 0.1rem -0.02rem color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 44%, transparent), 0 0.1rem 0.18rem -0.08rem color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 30%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Press disc sunk on press — near-flat contact only.

shadows.name: band-wrap
shadows.purpose: The obi band's folded head/foot edge — a bevel, not a lift.

motion.name: spring-release
motion.purpose: Underdamped spring (zeta 0.42, ~23% overshoot) driving the press disc's release/hover transform, 620ms. Press itself uses a fast unsprung ease-out instead — going down is instant, only the release rings.

motion.name: digit-roll
motion.purpose: A changed count digit's roll-and-settle: translateY + opacity + blur, iOS numeric-switcher style. Only changed digits animate.

motion.name: digit-stagger
motion.purpose: Leftmost changed digit animates first, cascading rightward across the number.

motion.name: disc-press
motion.purpose: Fast, unsprung press-down transition — deliberately not the spring.

components.name: The Mark (Press Button)
components.description: The product's single primary action: a solid obi-red disc with a fiber-texture overlay. Caption sits below via absolute position so it never competes with the disc's silhouette.

components.name: Count Display
components.description: The eternal count in foil gold, fixed-width digit cells so a tick never reflows. Only changed digits animate, cascading left to right.
components.html: 14,0
components.css: .ds-count { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: center; gap: 0.02em; font-family: Anton, sans-serif; font-size: clamp(3.4rem, 15.5vw, 12rem); line-height: 0.84; color: #8a6220; transform: scaleX(0.9); } .ds-digit { display: inline-block; width: 0.58em; text-align: center; position: relative; } .ds-digit__v { display: block; padding-block: 0.42em; margin-block: -0.42em; } .ds-count__sep { width: 0.22em; } .ds-digit.is-rolling .ds-digit__v { animation: ds-roll 340ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) both; } @keyframes ds-roll { 0% { transform: translateY(0.22em); opacity: 0; filter: blur(0.07em); } 60% { opacity: 1; filter: blur(0.02em); } 100% { transform: translateY(0); opacity: 1; filter: blur(0); } }

components.name: Label (Micro Caption)
components.description: The recurring uppercase tracked-out annotation: count label, button caption, pane metadata, catalog, axis ticks. Always sits beside or beneath its subject, never as a pre-headline kicker.
components.css: .ds-label { font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-size: 0.6rem; letter-spacing: 0.2em; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 600; color: #111111; margin: 0; }

narrative.overview:
A Tokyo boutique-pop sleeve for a single, eternal number. The page is printed, not screened: two inks — cream stock and obi red — on a fine-tooth uncoated ground, with exactly one color allowed to behave like something other than ink: the gold foil the count is set in. Everything else is flat, square-cornered, and hairline-ruled, as if it came off a press rather than out of a UI kit. It refuses the category default of a glowing counter centered on a dark ground with a pill button beneath it — here the ground is bare and light, the button is a single printed disc, and depth is earned by one real cast shadow rather than borrowed from gradients or glow.

The system is dense with meaning-bearing micro-copy (catalog numbers, vertical Japanese credit columns, a barcode, a colophon) but never decorative kicker copy — every small-caps line names the number, control, or fact sitting beside it. The signature device is the obi band itself: a wrapped, textured red band that crosses the bottom of the hero and unwraps into a full-width credits strip as the visitor scrolls, built with Canvas UI's Cloth (html-in-canvas WebGL drape) as a progressive enhancement over a flat CSS/SVG weave that is always present and always legible on its own.
keyCharacteristics: Two-ink print palette (cream + obi red) plus one foil ink reserved for the count alone
Anton display type, mechanically squeezed, never used below title scale; Archivo for everything readable
Exactly one rounded shape in the whole system — the press disc — against square corners everywhere else
One real elevation: a soft, two-layer cast shadow on the press disc; everything else is flat print or an inset "fold" bevel
Scroll-snap panes (100svh hero, ~52svh panes after) with a printed band that wraps and unwraps as the mechanism of scroll

rules.name: The One Foil Rule
rules.body: Foil gold is spent in exactly one place: the eternal count, at display scale. It does not repeat as a small-text color or a general accent; the build's one confirmed use below display scale (the .share__tag chip at 0.55rem, cream-on-foil) is a carried defect, not a pattern to extend.

rules.name: The One Ghost Rule
rules.body: Risograph red exists only inside the misregistration effect on the record chart. A future surface that wants a "second red" should not reach for #ff2a5b; it isn't a palette color, it's a printing artifact.

rules.name: The Anton-Only Display Rule
rules.body: Condensed display type never appears below title scale (~1.15rem). Body copy and every label are always Archivo — the system never uses the display face for anything meant to be read at length or at small size.

rules.name: The Half-Pane Rule
rules.body: The hero is always a full 100svh. Every following pane snaps to roughly half a viewport (~52svh desktop, 56svh mobile) — panes are deliberately incomplete at rest, inviting the next scroll rather than presenting a full "page."

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: Exactly one element in the system casts a real, non-inset shadow: the press disc. Every other surface is flat print or conveyed with an inset fold. A future component should not add ambient card shadows to match generic UI conventions — that vocabulary doesn't exist here.

dos: Do reserve foil gold (#8a6220) for the eternal count at display scale — the system's one emissive-reading color.
Do keep Anton confined to display/headline/title scale (≥~1.15rem); everything smaller is Archivo.
Do set every annotative label in uppercase Archivo, 0.55–0.62rem, 0.17–0.26em tracking, and place it beside or beneath the figure it names — never above a headline as a pre-announcement.
Do give the press disc a soft, two-layer cast shadow (contact + ambient) for its rest/hover/active states; use the documented exact values, not a generic drop-shadow.
Do keep corners square everywhere except the press disc; 50% radius is spent in exactly one place.
Do keep the obi band's flat CSS/SVG weave as the real, always-rendered surface; treat Cloth strictly as an enhancement layered on top, scoped to band elements only.
donts: Don't use risograph red (#ff2a5b) as a general secondary accent — it is confined to the single misregistration-ghost effect on the record chart.

Don't repeat the foil-on-small-text pattern from .share__tag (cream text on foil gold at 0.55rem). Its contrast was never machine-verified (detect.mjs ran degraded for this build) and it reads noticeably weaker than the rest of the label system — it is a carried defect from this build, not a system rule for new surfaces.
Don't add a hard-offset, high-contrast "neobrutalist" shadow anywhere in this system; its only elevation vocabulary is the soft two-layer cast shadow on the disc and the inset fold on the band.

Don't reuse the scaleX(0.86)/scaleX(0.9) horizontal squeeze on body copy, labels, or any non-Anton, non-display-scale type — it's a corrective specific to Anton at large sizes, not a general transform.
Don't invent a second button style (ghost, outline, secondary); the product has exactly one action and the system reflects that with exactly one button.
